headline: Tech sell-off deepens: AI credit worries sink chips for an eighth day while oil tops $100
summary: A risk-off session aimed squarely at the AI trade. Indexes were steady in the morning, then selling built through the afternoon and peaked in the last hour. Money rotated into energy and defensives, so the equal-weight S&P 500 fell only 0.4% and the Dow held up far better than the Nasdaq.
drivers: CoreWeave fell 11.9% as some of its bonds traded near 79 cents on the dollar (about $51B of debt); it lost 25% on the week. Goldman says spreads on AI-related high-yield debt hit a record 360bp, so data-center names (Applied Digital, IREN, Nebius) led the losers.

The SOX fell for an eighth straight session, down about 16% since Oct 6. AMD −6.0%, Intel −5.8%, Micron −5.6% (after China's CXMT announced a DRAM advance), Broadcom −4.5%, Sandisk −6.9%. Software joined in: Twilio −10.6%, Oracle −5%.

WTI settled above $100 for the first time in a month and Brent hit $109.86, its highest close since May, on Hormuz/Iran tensions and Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries. Energy (+2.5%) was the top sector.

Utilities +1.3%, staples +1.1% and financials gained (JPMorgan about +2%). The 2-year yield fell 3bp to 4.74% and the dollar slipped, but the S&P 500 and Nasdaq both closed below their 50-day averages and the VIX briefly topped 22, a four-month high.
week: Week: Nasdaq −4.5% (worst since June, ending a four-week win streak), S&P 500 −1.9%, Dow +0.7%. Hotter September CPI (3.7%) and PPI set a cautious tone earlier in the week.
watch: Next: whether AI credit spreads stabilise, oil and the Fed's October decision (hike odds eased to about 17%), and Big Tech results starting with Meta on Oct 21.
